main_body: A flat ground patch of dark olive-green gothic-style ground tiles, repeating a 16px pattern with small dark clumps, light speckles and a few orange/red dots. It is terrain with no standing volume.
top_band: none (flat ground texture; the repeating bands in the column scan are texture clumps, not a top surface)
evidence: The kind is terrain, so this is a ground patch rather than a standing object. The 3/4 top-plus-front structure does not apply. The column scan shows only a repeating 16-row texture of dark clumps and light speckles with no top band or front face, as expected for flat ground. No side face or object volume is drawn, so there is no 3/4 violation.

style.evidence: The candidate has 8 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile. The grass reference has 80 colours and 26 per tile, and the paving reference has 7 colours and 7 per tile. It is well below the grass but on par with the paving, so the density sits between the two references. The pattern has about 4 lightness steps: a dark mid-olive base, darker clumps, lighter speckles and a few accent dots. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no flat areas. The pattern repeats mechanically every 16px, with identical clumps and accent dots in every tile, which reads as a stamped texture and not hand-shaded grain. There is no outline and the dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so there is no sticker look. Shading is shallower than Beodeul's 5-6 steps and the colour count is far below the grass reference, so I judge it thinner than the reference of the same kind.
